scope: Offline MainOS firmware revision fallback; no fresh phone access

reference.decoder: Python standard-library gzip, UTF-16 and ElementTree XML

native_full_image_checks.label: Image fingerprint
native_full_image_checks.message: Complete local file SHA-256 recorded for later revalidation.

native_full_image_checks.label: Chunk integrity
native_full_image_checks.message: FFU SHA-256 chunk table checked; this does not authenticate the signing catalog.

native_full_image_checks.label: Catalog signature
native_full_image_checks.message: RSA/SHA-256 catalog signature and signed attributes verified. This does not establish signer trust or device acceptance.

native_full_image_checks.label: Signed hash-table binding
native_full_image_checks.message: Signed catalog member matches the FFU hash table using legacy SHA-1. Legacy collision resistance is not a modern authenticity guarantee.

native_full_image_checks.label: Firmware signer trust
native_full_image_checks.message: An embedded certificate is not a trust anchor. OEM chain, device root-key binding, certificate policy/time and revocation have not been validated.

checks.label: Installed / image firmware
checks.message: The image is numerically older within the same firmware branch. No downgrade acceptance/profile is validated; recovery remains blocked.

checks.label: Recovery execution
checks.message: Stock recovery currently runs only in protocol replay tests. No physical-device executor is enabled.

limits: The supported fallback requires matching Nokia registry and DSM packages; it does not parse registry hives or prove staged metadata equals the live registry.
PLAT is preferred when present; the fallback does not cross-check MainOS in that case.
Older same-branch metadata fails preparation because downgrade acceptance is unvalidated; this does not prove the phone would reject the image.
OEM trust, exact applicability, data preservation and a physical recovery executor remain unresolved.
Browser full-image chunk verification and fingerprinting remain unverified; synchronous MainOS lookup cancellation occurs at batch boundaries.
Only metadata and hashes are published. No proprietary package bytes, firmware, personal paths or USB identifiers are retained.
